messages:
maya: Heads up — eu-west1 GPU pool is seeing a cluster of ephemeral drives (2TB series) that are briefly pausing writes during heavy cleanup windows. Not all nodes, ~12/420 in the pool.

tom: Seen it. Symptoms? attach failures or just slower GPU attach times?

maya: Primarily attach stalls. GPU jobs hang waiting for pod start, kube shows container creating. dmesg on affected hosts shows repeated: 

leo: ```
[ 1234.567890] nvme0: I/O 0xabc123 failed, status: 0x2 
[ 1234.568001] nvme0n1: write timeout, stalled for 12000 ms
[ 1234.568012] nvme0: ctrl: reset start
```

maya: Drives are all same firmware cohort (FW: 5.4.1) and serial range S2K-7xxxxx. Non-2TB drives in same racks fine.

ana: Any recent daemonset or kernel updates? overlayfs/trim jobs?

maya: We rolled a cleaner tuning change yesterday that increases concurrency for scrub jobs during off-peak windows — likely overlap with attach spikes.

tom: Can we repro by running concurrent scrub on a canary host? If it's scrub concurrency -> write path contention.

leo: I started a repro on an isolated host and hit a write stall after ~45m of scrub at ~1800 iops. Looks like the controller resets then reinitializes, kube sees volume temporarily readonly.

ops-oncall: 🚨 We're throttling new GPU requests into eu-west1 for now. Routing policy bumped to prefer us-west2 for non-data-local workloads.

maya: Quick mitigation: reduce scrub concurrency on affected fleets, and add a temporary scrub backoff for hosts with serial prefix S2K-7. Also pushing kernel nvme_opts: io_timeout=60000? Might help avoid attach returns as IO errors.

tom: Agree. Also propose to patch the provisioner to detect "nvme reset" in the attach logs and retry with backoff + move to different host if persists. Low-risk change.

leo: Filed a short-lived canary: scrub concurrency -> 2 on eu-west1-ephemeral group and added statefulset to postpone scheduled scrub for hosts with that serial prefix. Monitoring graphs show attach latencies down from 18s -> 3s on canary.

maya: Nice. Can we also collect SMART / telemetry for that serial cohort and correlate temperature/thermal throttling?

leo: Pulling SMART now and opening a telemetry slice. Early look: no obvious SMART errors but power cycles align with controller resets.

deploy-bot: Reminder: rolling kernel bump to 5.10.132 is scheduled in 6h for eu-west1. Consider delaying until we validate this mitigation.

ops-oncall: Please hold the kernel roll — we've paused non-critical node updates. I'll notify infra-schedule.

ana: Cost question — routing to us-west2 increases egress/infra cost and may degrade latency for some customers. Ops: what's our current extra-cost estimate if this keeps up for 24h?

ops-oncall: Rough calc: extra cross-region allocation + higher preemptible churn ~ $2k/day for eu-west1->us-west2 redirection at current load. I'll include in incident notes.

maya: Next steps: 1) Keep scrub concurrency low for S2K-7 cohort 2) Collect full dmesg + SMART for affected hosts 3) Patch provisioner retry/backoff 4) Hold kernel roll 5) Telemetry correlation + vendor support reachout for FW 5.4.1.

tom: I'll own the provisioner patch, will submit PR within 2h and schedule a canary deploy.

leo: I'll hand over telemetry bundle + attach traces to vendor ticket.

ops-oncall: I'll update status in #incidents and ping support teams + the oncall rotation.

maya: Thanks — will monitor and post updates here. :thumbsup:
